facts.statement: Kotasaurus was discovered in the Kota Formation of Telangana, India.
facts.quote: It was discovered in the Kota Formation of Telangana, India

facts.statement: Remains of at least 12 individual Kotasaurus have been found.
facts.quote: So far the remains of at least 12 individuals are known.

facts.statement: The skull of Kotasaurus is missing except for two teeth.
facts.quote: the skull is missing, with the exception of two teeth.

facts.statement: P.M. Yadagiri named and described Kotasaurus yamanpalliensis in 1988.
facts.quote: In 1988 they were named and described by P.M. Yadagiri as a new genus and species of sauropod, Kotasaurus yamanpalliensis.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Kotasaurus is an ilium cataloged as 21/SR/PAL.
The Geological Survey of India assembled a skeletal mount of Kotasaurus for display at the Birla Science Museum in Hyderabad.
facts.quote: The Geological Survey of India combined several elements into a skeletal mount and displayed it at the Birla Science Museum, Hyderabad.

facts.statement: Kotasaurus lived during the Early Jurassic period, specifically from the Sinemurian to Pliensbachian stages.
facts.quote: Kotasaurus ( ; meaning "Kota Formation lizard") is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Early Jurassic period (Sinemurian–Pliensbachian).

facts.statement: Kotasaurus lived approximately between 196.5 and 183 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente entre 196,5 a 183 millones de años, desde el Sinemuriense al Pliensbachiense

facts.statement: The time range for Kotasaurus is estimated from 199.5 to 184.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Sinemurian to Pliensbachian (199.5 to 184.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Kotasaurus possessed a tail club likely used for fighting other Kotasaurus or defending against predators.
facts.quote: Like some sauropods, it had a tail club that would have been used for intraspecific combat or interspecific defense.

facts.statement: Kotasaurus had an estimated body length of nine meters and a weight of 2.5 tonnes.
facts.quote: The body length is estimated at nine meters, with a weight of 2.5 tonnes
La longitud del cuerpo se estima en aproximadamente 9 metros de largo, 3 de alto y pesaba alrededor de 2,5 toneladas.

facts.statement: Kotasaurus had spoon-shaped teeth similar to those of later sauropods.
facts.quote: The teeth were spoon-shaped, like those of later sauropods.

facts.statement: Unique features of Kotasaurus include relatively slender limb bones and a low, elongated preacetabular process on the ilium.
facts.quote: Autapomorphies (newly acquired features) include the relatively slender limb bones as well as the low and elongated preacetabular process (the forward-pointing process of the ilium).

facts.statement: Kotasaurus shared its habitat with the related dinosaur Barapasaurus.
facts.quote: shared its habitat with the related Barapasaurus.

facts.statement: A 2024 study identified four tail clubs among nearly 400 bones from at least 12 individuals of Kotasaurus.
facts.quote: Based on comparisons with sauropods that possess tail clubs (Omeisaurus and Shunosaurus), a 2024 study reported the presence of four tail clubs from among the nearly 400 bones belonging to at least 12 individuals of Kotasaurus with varying ontogenetic stage.

facts.statement: It was initially debated whether Kotasaurus was a true sauropod or a basal sauropodomorph outside the Sauropoda.
facts.quote: Initially, it was not clear if Kotasaurus represented a true sauropod or a basal sauropodomorph that has to be classified outside Sauropoda.

facts.statement: The exact phylogenetic relationships of Kotasaurus remain unclear.
facts.quote: The exact relationships are not entirely clear, however.

rejected.quote: These finds, altogether 840 skeletal parts, were found in the late 1970s.

rejected.quote: Today Kotasaurus is recognized as one of the most basal sauropods known.
